Sales increased 7.6 per cent to SEK 22,288 (20,717) million in the first nine months of the year, driven by organic growth and acquisitions. All business areas except Dental reported organic growth. The increase in sales was especially strong in Transportation Products and Systems Solutions as a result of acquisitions. Exchange rate effects negatively impacted sales for the period.

EBITA increased 10.3 per cent to SEK 5,072 (4,600) million and the EBITA margin expanded by 0.6 percentage points to 22.8 (22.2) per cent as a result of acquisitions and organic growth. The improvement in profitability was particularly strong in Dental and Systems Solutions, while a negative product mix continued to impact Demolition & Tools. The increase in Dental’s profitability was driven by acquisitions with high margins and a positive product mix. In Systems Solutions, organic growth in all divisions as well as acquisitions contributed to the improvement in profitability.
Earnings per share increased 11.7% till SEK 6.38 (5.71) during the first nine months of the year. Cash flow from operating activities increased 12.0 per cent to SEK 3,514 (3,138) million.

Lifco consolidated the Italian companies Boscaro and Metalltech, the UK companies Ethoss Regeneration and Glass Umbrella, the German companies Karl Kaps and Mozelt and the French company ErgoPack France during the first nine months of the year. The companies are highly specialised and jointly have sales of about SEK 670 million.

In July, Lifco updated its MTN programme with a loan framework of SEK 8 billion, and in August, Lifco issued an unsecured bond of SEK 750 million. Lifco thereby has bonds outstanding totalling SEK 4,500 million. Lifco’s financial position remains strong and interest-bearing net debt amounted to 1.0 times EBITDA at 30 September 2026, which is well in line with our target of interest-bearing net debt of a maximum of three times EBITDA. This means that Lifco possesses the financial scope to make additional acquisitions.

Net sales increased 7.6 per cent to SEK 22,288 (20,717) million, with growth in all business areas. Acquisitions contributed 6.6 per cent and organic growth amounted to 2.5 per cent. Exchange rate effects had a negative impact on sales of 1.5 per cent. The Italian companies Boscaro and Metalltech, the UK companies Ethoss Regeneration and Glass Umbrella, the German companies Karl Kaps and Mozelt and the French company ErgoPack France were consolidated during the period.

EBITA increased 10.3 per cent to SEK 5,072 (4,600) million and the EBITA margin improved 0.6 percentage points to 22.8 (22.2) per cent due to increased profitability in all business areas except Demolition & Tools and Transportation Products.

Exchange rate changes had a negative impact on EBITA of 1.3 per cent. During the period, 47 (46) per cent of EBITA was generated in EUR, 14 (17) per cent in SEK, 16 (14) per cent in GBP, 11 (9) per cent in NOK, 6 (6) per cent in DKK, 2 (3) per cent in USD and 4 (4) per cent in other currencies.
Net financial items improved to SEK -249 (-317) million.
Profit before tax grew 14.4 per cent to SEK 3,932 (3,437) million. Net profit for the period grew 11.7 per cent to SEK 2,930 (2,624) million.
Average capital employed excluding goodwill increased SEK 578 million during the period, to SEK

5,348 million at 30 September 2026, compared with SEK 4,770 million at 31 December 2025. EBITA in relation to average capital employed excluding goodwill decreased 5 percentage points from the end of the year to 127 per cent.

The Group’s net debt increased SEK 273 million from 31 December 2025 to SEK 12,321 million at 30 September 2026, of which liabilities related to put/call options for acquisitions decreased SEK 212 million to SEK 2,718 million from SEK 2,930 million at year-end. Interest-bearing net debt increased during the nine-month period by SEK 178 million to SEK 7,979 million, compared to SEK 7,801 million at 31 December 2025.

In July 2026, Lifco updated its MTN programme with a loan framework of SEK 8 billion, and in August 2026, Lifco issued an unsecured bond of SEK 750 million, with a maturity of two years and an annual variable interest rate of 3-month STIBOR +0.45%. Lifco thereby has bonds outstanding totalling SEK 4,500 million. The terms of the MTN programme and bonds are available on lifco.se. In addition to bonds outstanding, Lifco has standard short-term credit facilities.

The net debt/equity ratio as of 30 September 2026 amounted to 0.6 (0.7), compared with 0.6 at year-end. Net debt in relation to EBITDA was 1.6 (1.9) times compared to 1.7 times at the end of the year. Interest-bearing net debt in relation to EBITDA was 1.0 (1.3) times compared to 1.1 times at the end of the year.

Cash flow from operating activities increased 12.0 per cent to SEK 3,514 (3,138) million during the period. Cash flow from investing activities was SEK -1,761 (-3,243) million, which was mainly attributable to acquisitions.
GROUP PERFORMANCE IN THE THIRD QUARTER

Sales increased 8.3 per cent to SEK 7,407 (6,842) million in the third quarter due to higher sales in all business areas. Acquisitions contributed 5.6 per cent and organic growth amounted to 1.6 per cent. Exchange rate changes had a positive impact on sales of 1.1 per cent.
EBITA increased 10.7 per cent to SEK 1,708 (1,543) million and the EBITA margin grew 0.5 percentage points to 23.1 (22.6) per cent due to increased profitability in Dental and Systems Solutions.

Exchange rate changes had a positive impact on EBITA of 1.1 per cent. During the third quarter, 47 (43) per cent of EBITA was generated in EUR, 14 (17) per cent in SEK, 16 (16) per cent in GBP, 10 (9) per cent in NOK, 7 (7) per cent in DKK, 2 (3) per cent in USD and 4 (4) per cent in other currencies.
Net financial items improved to SEK -78 (-111) million.

Profit before tax grew 17.7 per cent to SEK 1,323 (1,124) million. Net profit for the period grew 9.5 per cent to SEK 986 (900) million. The comparison for net profit for the period is impacted by a lower-than-normal effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2025 due to a reduction in the corporate tax rate in Germany.

Average capital employed excluding goodwill increased SEK 217 million to SEK 5,348 million at 30 September 2026, compared with SEK 5,131 million at 30 June 2026. EBITA in relation to average capital employed excluding goodwill amounted to 127 per cent at 30 September 2026 and to 129 per cent at 30 June 2026.

The Group’s net debt decreased SEK 1,027 million from 30 June 2026 to SEK 12,321 million, of which liabilities related to put/call options for acquisitions decreased SEK 69 million from 30 June 2026 to SEK 2,718 million.

Cash flow from operating activities increased 19.2 per cent to SEK 1,662 (1,394) million. Cash flow from investing activities was SEK -390 (-1,614) million, which was mainly attributable to acquisitions.

The companies in Lifco’s Dental business area are leading suppliers of consumables, equipment and technical service to dentists across Europe, and the business area also has operations in the US. Lifco sells dental technology to dentists in the Nordic countries and Germany, and develops and sells medical record systems in Denmark, Sweden and Germany. The business area also includes a number of manufacturers which produce, inter alia, fitting products for dentures, disinfectants, saliva ejectors, bite registration and dental impression materials, bonding agents and other consumables that are sold to dentists through distributors around the world.
Net sales in Dental increased 3.7 per cent to SEK 4,911 (4,737) million during the first nine months of the year due to acquisitions.

EBITA increased 10.1 per cent to SEK 1,115 (1,013) million during the nine-month period. The EBITA margin improved 1.3 percentage points to 22.7 (21.4) per cent as a result of acquisitions with high margins and positive mix effects from strong performances in manufacturing companies during the period.

The British company Ethoss Regeneration, which markets and sells regenerative bone graft material to dentists and facial surgeons, and the German company Karl Kaps, a niche manufacturer of medical and dental microscopes, were consolidated in January 2026.

The Demolition & Tools business area develops, manufactures and sells equipment for the infrastructure, demolition and construction industries. The Group is the world’s leading supplier in the markets for demolition robots and crane attachments. The Group is also one of the leading global suppliers of attachments for forest machinery and excavators. The business area’s EBITA margin might fluctuate between quarters due to single, major special orders and changes to the product mix.
Sales increased 0.9 per cent during the first nine months of the year to SEK 5,127 (5,081) million. Organic growth in the period was counteracted by negative exchange rate effects.

EBITA decreased 3.6 per cent to SEK 1,236 (1,283) million during the nine-month period and the EBITA margin decreased 1.2 percentage points to 24.1 (25.3) per cent, primarily as a result of a weak market trend for demolition robots that led to a negative product mix in the period.

The Italian company Boscaro, a niche designer and manufacturer of construction equipment and crane attachments, and the Germany company Mozelt, which designs and manufactures generators and magnet systems for material handling, were consolidated in July 2026.
The Environmental Technology business area offers solutions that improve working environments and reduce environmental impact in the marine sector, industrial processes and recycling.
Sales increased 4.4 per cent to SEK 2,625 (2,514) million in the first nine months of the year, driven by organic growth.

During the nine-month period, EBITA increased 7.7 per cent to SEK 715 (663) million and the EBITA margin improved 0.8 percentage points to 27.2 (26.4) per cent, primarily as a result of organic growth.

ErgoPack France was consolidated in September 2026. Since ErgoPack France is a distributor for the Lifco company ErgoPack Deutschland, the acquisition will have a very limited impact on Lifco’s consolidated external sales.
The Transportation Products business area offers solutions and accessories for service and transport vehicles as well as material handling within industrial applications.
Sales increased 19.4 per cent to SEK 3,207 (2,687) million in the first nine months of the year as the result of acquisitions and organic growth.
During the nine-month period, EBITA increased 19.0 per cent to SEK 722 (606) million and the EBITA margin decreased 0.1 percentage point to 22.5 (22.6) per cent.

Through its operating units, the Systems Solutions business area operates in industries offering systems solutions. Systems Solutions is divided into three divisions: Contract Manufacturing, Infrastructure Products and Special Products.
Sales in Systems Solutions increased 12.6 per cent to SEK 6,418 (5,699) million during the first nine months of the year due to acquisitions and organic growth.

EBITA increased 23.8 per cent during the nine-month period to SEK 1,445 (1,167) million and the EBITA margin expanded by 2.0 percentage points to 22.5 (20.5) per cent as a result of acquisitions and organic growth.

Contract Manufacturing reported a stable sales trend with improved profitability in the nine-month period as the result of organic growth and acquisitions. A customer in the Contract Manufacturing division, accounting for approximately 5 per cent of Lifco’s total revenue, has reduced its forecasts as of January 2027 and announced its intention to shift purchases to other suppliers outside Europe. This is expected to have a negative impact on System Solution’s revenue and earnings in 2027.

Sales and profitability in Infrastructure Products increased during the nine-month period due to acquisitions and organic growth. The Italian company Metalltech, which designs and manufactures expanded metal mesh for architectural applications, was consolidated in April 2026, and the UK company Glass Umbrella, a niche manufacturer of secondary glazing, was consolidated in May 2026.
Special Products reported a healthy performance in sales in the first nine months of the year as a result of acquisitions and organic growth. Profitability was unchanged.

New business area heads and members of Group Management Team

On 8 September 2026, Lifco announced that Jonas Redin had been appointed as the Head of Business Area Dental, Thomas Friedrich as Head of Business Area Demolition & Tools, and Josef Alenius as Head of Business Area Systems Solutions. Josef Alenius succeeded Martin Linder, who decided to leave Lifco in spring 2027 to focus on his own business. All three are members of the Group Management Team.
Events after the end of the reporting period

Consolidation of the Italian company Micronova will take place in the fourth quarter of 2026 in the Systems Solutions business area, division Contract Manufacturing. Micronova develops and manufactures customised electronic boards and touch screen displays sold to OEMs in various industries. In 2025, Micronova reported sales of approximately EUR 35.1 million and has 49 employees. The acquisition, which comprised all of the shares, was announced on 28 September 2026.

Consolidation of the German company Hega Medical will take place in the fourth quarter of 2026 in the Dental business area. Hega Medical manufactures products for cleaning of medical equipment for laboratories, clinics and hospitals. In 2025, Hega Medical reported sales of approximately EUR 1.6 million and has ten employees. The acquisition, which comprised all of the shares, was announced on 15 October 2026.
During the period, customary transactions with related parties have occurred. All transactions have been carried out on market terms.

The risk factors which have the biggest impact for Lifco are global macroeconomic and geopolitical factors, the competitive situation, structural changes in the market and general level of economic activity. Lifco is also exposed to financial risks, including currency risks, interest rate risks, credit and counterparty risks. Lifco is working actively to monitor and continually evaluate sustainability-related risks and their impact on the Group’s operations and earnings. The Group has established a governance structure that involves the Group Management Team and the Board and works to continually improve the company’s sustainability-related activities and minimise related risks. As part of this governance, the Group Management Team evaluates the compliance of, for example, the Code of Conduct, occupational injuries, IT security and legal disputes, for every subsidiary on a quarterly basis. The risks and sensitivity analysis are described in detail in Lifco’s 2025 Annual and Sustainability Report and have remained unchanged since this report.
The Parent Company is affected by the above risks and uncertainties in its capacity as owner of the subsidiary companies.

The Group’s interim report has been prepared in accordance with IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting and the Swedish Annual Accounts Act. In respect of the Parent Company, the report has been prepared in accordance with the Annual Accounts Act and Recommendation RFR 2 Financial Reporting for Legal Entities of the Swedish Financial Reporting Board. The accounting policies have been applied in accordance with those which are presented in the 2025 Annual Report and should be read in conjunction with these.

IFRS 18 enters into force 1 January 2027 and will impact the presentation and disclosures in the Group’s financial statements. Management is continuing to evaluate the impact the new standards will have on the consolidated financial statements. No material impact on the Group’s financial position or earnings has been identified at this stage.

At the beginning of the second quarter of 2026, Lifco decided to reorganise into five operating segments instead of the previous three. This change was made after many years of strong growth in Systems Solutions through acquisitions and organic growth. Within Systems Solutions, the two divisions Environmental Technology and Transportation Products, have become so material that from the second quarter of 2026 they are reported and monitored internally by the chief operating decision-maker. As of the second quarter of 2026, Systems Solutions consists of the Contract Manufacturing, Infrastructure Products and Special Products divisions. The Dental and Demolition & Tools operating segments are not affected by the change. The report for the first quarter of 2026 presented sales, EBITA and EBITA margin per quarter 2024–2026 and the full years 2015–2025 for the new business areas Environmental Technology and Transportation Products as well as Systems Solutions excluding Environmental Technology and Transportation Products.

Seven new operations were acquired during the first nine months of the year, which were announced via press releases: the Italian companies Boscaro and Metalltech, the UK companies Ethoss Regeneration and Glass Umbrella, the German companies Karl Kaps and Mozelt and the French company ErgoPack France. The majority of the shares were acquired in Boscaro, Ethoss Regeneration, Metalltech and Glass Umbrella, while all shares were acquired in ErgoPack France, Karl Kaps and Mozelt. Where the majority of shares were acquired, combined put/call options were issued to the sellers.

Minor bolt-on acquisitions have not been announced via press releases. However, the purchase price allocation includes all acquisitions consolidated in the nine-month period. All acquisitions have been consolidated at 100 percent.

Acquisition-related expenses of SEK 18 million are included in administrative expenses in the consolidated income statement for the first nine months of the year. Since the respective consolidation dates, the acquired companies have added SEK 282 million to consolidated net sales and SEK 83 million to EBITA. If the businesses had been consolidated as of 1 January 2026, net sales for the year would have increased a further SEK 222 million and EBITA would have increased a further SEK 51 million.

Financial instruments at fair value are classified into different levels depending on how fair value is determined. All financial instruments at fair value in the Lifco Group have been classified as level 3, i.e. unobservable inputs. The put/call options are valued on the basis of a multiple valuation whereby a contractually determined multiple according to the terms of the contracts is applied to average EBITA/EBIT for the three immediately preceding financial years before the options can be exercised/expire.

As of 30 September 2026, there were 52 option agreements (57 as of 31 December 2025), and the median value of the holdings relating to put/call options amounted to 20 per cent (20 per cent 31 December 2025) of the shares in each subsidiary. No individual option agreement has or could have a material impact on Lifco’s financial statements. The specification of the liability associated with these agreements was as follows: 81 per cent in EUR, 15 per cent in GBP, 3 per cent in DKK, and the remaining 1 per cent in SEK and NOK. The multiples ranged from 3.5x to 8.25x. The put/call options as of 30 September 2026 expire between 2026 and 2037.

The uncertainty in the valuation can be found in the assessment of future EBITA/EBIT until the maturity date and changes in exchange rates. Revaluation takes place on every balance sheet date based on the EBITA/EBIT for the most recent twelve months for each subsidiary. A 10 per cent change in EBITA/EBIT for all option agreements would affect the liability by approximately SEK 221 million (SEK 200 million as of 31 December 2025), corresponding to 1 per cent of equity. Higher EBITA/EBIT results in a higher liability and vice versa. A reasonably possible 10 per cent change in foreign exchange rates in relation to the SEK would affect the liability by approximately SEK 270 million (SEK 280 million as of 31 December 2025), corresponding to 1 per cent of equity. Stronger foreign exchange rates in relation to the SEK result in a higher liability and vice versa.

The sensitivity analysis is calculated by applying a percentage change to each unobservable input and calculating the resulting effect on the fair value of the liability. The analyses assume that all other variables remain constant.

EBITA is a measure which Lifco considers relevant for investors who wish to understand the earnings generated after investments in tangible and intangible assets requiring reinvestment but before investments in intangible assets attributable to acquisitions. Lifco defines earnings before interest, tax and amortisation (EBITA) as operating profit before amortisation and impairment of intangible assets arising from acquisitions excluding acquisition costs.

EBITDA is a measure which Lifco considers relevant for investors who wish to understand the earnings generated before investments in non-current assets. Lifco defines earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) as operating profit before depreciation, amortisation and impairment of tangible and intangible assets excluding acquisition costs.

Lifco uses the alternative KPI net debt. Lifco considers that this is a useful additional KPI which allows users of the financial statements to assess the Group’s ability to pay dividends, make strategic investments and meet its financial obligations. Lifco defines the KPI as follows: current and non-current liabilities to credit institutions, bonds, interest-bearing pension provisions, liabilities related to put/call options relating to acquisitions as well as lease liabilities less cash and cash equivalents.
Profit after tax attributable to Parent Company shareholders, divided by the average number of shares outstanding.

Lifco uses the alternative KPI interest-bearing net debt. Lifco considers that this is a useful additional KPI which allows users of the financial statements to assess the Group’s ability to pay dividends, make strategic investments and meet its financial obligations. Lifco defines the KPI as follows: current and non-current liabilities to credit institutions, bonds as well as interest-bearing pension provisions less cash and cash equivalents.
Equity divided by total assets (balance sheet total).

Capital employed is a measure which Lifco uses for calculating the return on capital employed and for measuring how efficient the Group is. Lifco considers that capital employed is useful in helping users of the financial statements to understand how the Group finances itself. Lifco defines capital employed as total assets less cash and cash equivalents, interest-bearing pension provisions and non-interest-bearing liabilities with the exception of liabilities related to put/call options relating to acquisitions, calculated as the average of the last four quarters.

Capital employed excluding goodwill and other intangible assets is a measure which Lifco uses for calculating the return on capital employed and for measuring how efficient the Group is. Lifco considers that capital employed excluding goodwill and other intangible assets is useful in helping users of the financial statements to understand the impact of goodwill and other intangible assets on that capital which requires a return. Lifco defines capital employed excluding goodwill and other intangible assets as total assets less cash and cash equivalents, interest-bearing pension provisions, non-interest-bearing liabilities with the exception of liabilities related to put/call options relating to acquisitions, goodwill and other intangible assets, calculated as the average of the last four quarters.

Lifco offers a safe haven for small and medium-sized businesses. Lifco’s business concept is to acquire and develop market-leading niche businesses with the potential to deliver sustainable earnings growth and robust cash flows. Lifco is guided by a clear philosophy centred on long-term growth, a focus on profitability and a strongly decentralised organisation. The Group has five business areas: Dental, Demolition & Tools, Environmental Technology, Transportation Products and Systems Solutions. At year-end 2025, the Lifco Group consisted of 275 operating companies in 37 countries. In 2025, Lifco reported EBITA of SEK 6.3 billion on net sales of SEK 28.3 billion. The EBITA margin was 22.4 per cent. Read more at lifco.se.
